Status: reproduced. The bug is present at commit 327c67256fbeaf9d5e365802c2a11f5d32a16522, and I did not change any production code.

Command, run from the repo root:

    node recreate-19957.js

The script is `recreate-19957.js` in the repo root. It runs the `no-loss-of-precision` rule through `Linter` on `const test = <literal>;`. It exits 1 while any literal that is exactly representable gets reported, and exits 0 once none are.

What I saw (exit code 1):

    FAIL 9.000e+3  (= 9000) -> no-loss-of-precision: This number literal will lose precision at runtime.
    FAIL 9.000e3   (= 9000) -> no-loss-of-precision: This number literal will lose precision at runtime.
    FAIL 9.0000e4  (= 90000) -> no-loss-of-precision: This number literal will lose precision at runtime.
    ok   9.000e4   (= 90000) -> no report
    ok   9.0000e5  (= 900000) -> no report
    ok   9e3       (= 9000) -> no report
    ok   9000      (= 9000) -> no report

- **The reported input:** `9.000e+3` is flagged, though it is exactly 9000.
- **The maintainer's variants:** `9.000e3` and `9.0000e4` are flagged as well. This matches the accepted comment on the report.
- **Controls:** `9.000e4`, `9.0000e5`, `9e3` and `9000` are not flagged, so the check passes where the expected behavior already holds.

I also ran the real CLI, `node bin/eslint.js a.js`, in a scratch directory under /tmp. The config enables only `no-loss-of-precision`, and the file contains `const test = 9.000e+3 // 9000`. It printed `1:14 error This number literal will lose precision at runtime no-loss-of-precision` and exited 1.

The only thing I left in the working tree is `recreate-19957.js`.
